title: Open Courtesy Transportation Agreements per Customer and per Repair Order
content:
Desk guidance on the Courtesy Transportation Agreements limit on agreements out at the same time.

## Rule

1. A customer may have at most the program's maximum number of open agreements per customer of one program out at the same time.
2. That number is counted before the new agreement is issued. The count is the number of the customer's agreements of the same program that are in out status at the time of handling.
3. A new agreement may be issued only when that count is below the program's maximum of agreements out at once.
4. A retail customer with a loaner still out receives no second loaner until the first is returned.
5. One repair order supports at most one courtesy or warranty loaner at a time.

An agreement is in out status from the day the loaner is issued until it is checked back in, when its status becomes returned; a returned agreement is later closed.

## Decision table for clause 3

| Count of the customer's same-program agreements in out status | Compared with the program's maximum | Issue of a new agreement of that program |
|---|---|---|
| Below the maximum | Less | Allowed by this limit |
| Equal to the maximum | Not less | Not allowed |
| Above the maximum | Not less | Not allowed |

## What the count includes

- Only agreements in out status are counted; agreements already returned or closed are not.
- Only agreements of the same program as the new one are counted for clause 1.
- The count is taken as things stand at the time of handling, before the new agreement exists.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A program whose maximum is one agreement out at once: a customer with no agreement of that program in out status may be issued one (count 0, below 1); a customer whose agreement of that program is still out may not (count 1, equal to 1).
- A program whose maximum is five: a customer with four agreements of that program in out status may be issued a fifth (count 4, below 5); with five out, a sixth may not be issued (count 5, equal to 5).
- A repair order that already supports a courtesy loaner that is out does not support a second courtesy or warranty loaner at the same time.

The counts in these illustrations are invented for the example.
